source.b: Barbara McKeldin Adams, "Barbara McKeldin Adams - A Memoir" (privately printed)

facts.value: 9 Feb 1964 was the Sunday the Beatles appeared on the Ed Sullivan Show. George Harrison and John Lennon visited Mercy High later that week, when Barbara was a sophomore. She had started at Mercy as a freshman around fall 1962 (she was already a sophomore when JFK was shot in Nov 1963).
Barbara probably started at Towson State in fall 1966. She was in the Mercy High class that were sophomores in 1963-64, and she got her first job the summer before college.
Her bridesmaids were her high school and college friends Bea Rider, Julie Smith and Doris Rutkowski. Julie caught the bouquet.

The Army-Navy weekend when she and John first talked about marriage was at the end of November 1968. John's parents George and Beryl came, along with Ralph, Rosemary and Louise O'Dell, Pete and Betty O'Neil, and the O'Donalds. Barbara shared a hotel room with Uncle Ralph and Aunt Rosemary. Army won 21-14.

facts.place: Tilghman's Company, State Circle, Annapolis, MD
facts.value: She and John went diamond shopping in Annapolis in February 1969, after the Army-Navy weekend.
Right after the 31 Jan 1970 wedding she moved to Milton, Florida, John's first duty station. The drive there was their only honeymoon. They moved five times in their first three years of marriage.
Next they lived in Beeville, Texas, in an unfinished house that the owner, Henry Isler, let them have rent free if they fixed it up. Navy couple Cindy and Bob Riera lived next door.
In Meridian, Mississippi, she team-taught science and English at Kate Griffin Junior High. She got pregnant with Brian that summer and was let go because pregnant teachers were not allowed.
The family lived in Oak Harbor for two years while John flew from the USS Ranger. Barbara sat on the board of Brian's preschool and volunteered there two or three days a week.
They lived in Port Townsend for two and a half years after John left active duty.
They lived in Gilroy, California, for 18 months. At the same time her brother Chuck was at postgraduate school in Monterey.

In Vancouver, Washington, they rented at first and then bought a Victorian house next to the WSU campus. When John took the New Mexico job they sold it, and Barbara lived in an apartment in Vancouver before joining him in Crownpoint.
The research trip around Washington for her master's thesis (Master of Arts, Seattle Pacific) happened when Brendan was ten and Brian thirteen, which puts it around summer 1985.

Barbara had 26 male and 6 female first cousins. Her nearest girl cousin in age was Sharon, born when Barbara was ten (about 1958). Cousins she names include Quinn, Tommy, Mark, Tim, Michael, Sharon, John, Joanie, Matthew, Billy (Chuck's age) and Bobbie.
While at Lower Columbia College she taught a U.S. Government class at night to high school students, and also taught INDV 90, How To Succeed in College.

The family lived about one year in Redding, California, then moved back to the Pacific Northwest to an apartment in Vancouver, Washington; their dog Snickers died in 1996 while they were still in Redding.

She was hired in the University of Portland School of Education after interviewing with Ellyn Arwood, who became her boss, and Dean Sister Maria, and worked there about two years in the outreach master's program.

During her roughly three years as Running Start coordinator at Lower Columbia College she lived in Ridgefield, Washington, and commuted to Longview, while John worked away (driving truck, consulting, then in New Mexico).
She finished her quarter at Lower Columbia College and joined John in Crownpoint, New Mexico, in March 2005, after they had lived apart for two to three years.

At Crownpoint High School she was hired on the spot by the long-time principal Mr. (Bruce) Helms and worked four years under him; after he retired she stayed one more year and left when her five years were up in March.

When the Navy sent John to Beeville with 'no dependents' housing, they stayed two days in a hotel, then with a classmate of John's, then rented an unfinished house from landlord Henry Isler, finishing it in exchange for three months' free rent; she says they survived Hurricane Camille there.

facts.place: Kate Griffin Junior High, Meridian, MS
facts.value: One of her students at Kate Griffin Junior High was Brenda Chaney, sister of civil-rights worker James Chaney, who was murdered by the Klan for registering black voters.

Her running career began with Port Townsend's Rhodie Run; with friends Brent and Rosemary Shirley the family took a replica Victorian house float to parades around the Northwest for the Port Townsend Queen's Court, and she later ran the Gilroy Garlic Festival race.
Barbara lists the University of Portland among the schools she attended, alongside St. Dominic's, Mercy High, Towson State and Seattle Pacific.

In 1993 Barbara and John took an Alaskan cruise with Granny and Pops (her father and stepmother) and Nana and Bob, including a helicopter ride to the Mendenhall Glacier and a train ride up into the gold fields.

facts.place: Ireland; Vienna; Salzburg; Black Forest; Paris
facts.value: In 2012 Barbara and John took a bus tour of Ireland and the Continent, staying in Dublin, Vienna, Salzburg, the Black Forest and Paris.
In 2015 Barbara and John took a Caribbean cruise that sailed from Fort Lauderdale.
In 2016 Barbara and John took an ocean cruise around South America, starting with Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires, visiting the Falklands and Patagonia and rounding the tip of the continent.
In 2017 Barbara and John went to Mont Blanc to watch Brendan race the UTMB, then took a bus tour of Spain, Portugal and Gibraltar.

Barbara and John spent their 20th wedding anniversary on Maui; their other Hawaii trips included stays at the Hale Koa Hotel on Oahu, a Christmas trip, a whole-family trip, and trips with Trudy and with George and Cindy.

Barbara's heirlooms include a black-and-gold rocking chair that was Grandmother Quinn's wedding present, her brother Chuck's youth chair, and a pewter tea set her parents gave on their fifth wedding anniversary; John gave her a miniature Naval Academy class ring.

As a child Barbara went with her family to a Quaker family's furniture barn in Pennsylvania, where her parents chose the wood and design for two end tables and a coffee table, and the children drank sassafras root beer.
John became 'Uncle Hims' after his niece Jenny, Chuck's daughter, whom he and Barbara babysat over a long weekend, told her parents tearfully, 'Hims sent me to my room.'

One Saturday night in Kelso, already dressed in suit and tie for a formal dinner, John took the training wheels off Brendan's bike and ran up and down the road with him until he balanced; they still arrived on time.
John collects Hard Rock Cafe T-shirts from locations around the world; on the 2016 South America trip the tour guide let him off at a Hard Rock Cafe to get one.
At the Equator in Ecuador, John was the only one in the tour group who could balance an egg on the head of a nail, earning the title 'Egg Master'.
In Dublin, Barbara saved John's life twice when he looked the wrong way before crossing the street.
In retirement John golfs, goes to the driving range weekly, meets with two coffee groups each week, swims at 24 Hour Fitness, does the food shopping and makes dinner.
Went to preschool in Oak Harbor as a toddler.
Went to school in Gilroy, where his mother volunteered in his classroom (first grade) in the mornings.
Went to Catholic school in Kelso and graduated from high school while the family lived there.
Brian was baptized by the parish priest of the Navy base parish in Meridian, Mississippi.

Brian made his First Communion on the day Mount St. Helens erupted (Sunday, 18 May 1980), with Granny and Pops, Nana and Papa, and Aunt Rosemary and Uncle Ralph attending; he was also baptized, made his first confession and was confirmed.

After San Diego the family settled in a house on Whidbey Island, where John was soon deployed; there little Brian picked out two goldfish, named them Ernie and Bert, and was found lifting them out of the bowl onto the kitchen counter.
Brian entered St. Rose School in second grade when the family moved to Kelso, then went to Coweeman Junior High and Kelso High School, where he was a sophomore in 1988 and later graduated.

As a high school junior Brian went to Europe to play soccer with coach Cliff McCrath (ODP and Seattle Pacific University), and carried a crystal vase from Czechoslovakia home for his mother, packed in his socks and underwear.
In high school Brian made lifelong friends John Nordstrom, Mark McGee and David Schmaltz.

Getting the mower out, Brian put his mother's car in neutral and it rolled down the steep driveway, across the road and into the blackberries, which stopped it; he then dented it with an axe trying to chop the brambles away.

As a toddler dressed all in blue, Brian was taken for a girl by a stranger at the Mount Vernon mall and told her, 'You are a real winner, lady,' repeating what his mother had just said to a driver who stole her parking spot.
In high school Brian travelled to four countries to play soccer for coach Cliff McCrath, and brought his mother back a crystal vase stuffed with his underwear and socks so it would not break.
Went to preschool two mornings a week in Gilroy. A neighbour, Joyce Hinn, looked after him one more morning a week.
Went to Catholic school in Kelso and graduated from high school while the family lived there.
His middle name McKeldin was chosen by both parents as his mother's family name.
At his first birthday in Port Townsend, Nana and Papa gave him Clem, a toy hound dog as tall as he was, and he burst into tears; he never liked sleeping with stuffed animals.
Brendan went to preschool in Gilroy on days neighbour Joyce Hinn could not babysit him.
Brendan went to St. Rose School, was accepted into the DEEP program, where Chris Rabideau became his best buddy, then went to Coweeman Junior High and graduated from Kelso High School.
Though small for his age, Brendan wrestled and played basketball, soccer and football, and was quarterback of the Coweeman Junior High team, with Chris Rabideau at center.
Brendan took a quarter off from the University of Washington to travel all over Europe.
Brendan was baptized, made his first confession and First Communion, which Granny and Pops came west to attend, and was confirmed.
In 2017 Brendan ran the UTMB, the ultra-trail race around Mont Blanc, with his parents there to watch.
Barbara, born 12 Feb 1948, says she arrived 'a year and 8 days' after Chuck, which gives his birth as 4 Feb 1947.
Was at postgraduate school in Monterey while Barbara's family lived in Gilroy.

Chuck, Michele and Jenny lived in Monterey while Chuck was at postgraduate school, where the chaplain served naval graduate students (suggesting the Naval Postgraduate School); the Adamses in Gilroy visited them every other weekend, and son Charlie was born there.
Called Jenny. Her aunt Barbara babysat her over a long weekend while Chuck was at school in Monterey.
Jennifer was called Jenny.

As a small child, while her father was at postgraduate school in Monterey, Jenny stayed a long weekend with Uncle John and Aunt Barbara in Gilroy and, when her parents came, announced 'Hims sent me to my room', giving John the lasting nickname Uncle Hims.
His sisters called him 'Buckey'. His wife (Barbara's stepmother Peggy) hated the nickname and once said on the drive home from a visit that she would be sick if she heard 'Buckey' one more time.

He was not Catholic but went to church with his mother every Sunday, prayed kneeling by his bed every night, and paid for his children to go to Catholic school. He became Catholic while Barbara was in college.

He took the children to Orioles and Colts games, the Ringling Brothers circus and Barbara's Saturday duckpin bowling, and took them fishing on the Chesapeake Bay at Ocean City. Sunday country drives ended with ice cream if they behaved.
Brian and Brendan called him Pops (with Peggy as Granny).
Buckey and Peggy visited the Adamses out west every other year, came for both boys' First Communions, and stayed at their Kelso house for Mike and Shelley's wedding.
The family called him 'Pops', and he and Peggy were 'Granny and Pops' to the grandchildren.

He went to the Duck Carvers Convention in Ocean City and always came back with bird pins or decoys; he carved a few himself, including a swan and a Santa, and at his death Barbara split his decoys with her brothers.
With Peggy he went on the 1993 Alaska cruise with Barbara and John, and on a Hawaii trip with them and Nana that took in Oahu, Maui and the Big Island.
His favourite tree was the dogwood, and he gave Barbara a pinkie ring engraved with her initials BJM.
Went to Seton High School. This is why Barbara chose Mercy High instead.
Barbara describes her as 'quite the equestrian', and family photos show her at Ocean City.
The 'uncle the magician' Emily helped in an old photo is probably her uncle John Joseph Quinn, whom Barbara remembers doing magic tricks for the children.
Worked as a nurse after nursing school.
She was Roman Catholic. Because Buckey was not yet Catholic, their wedding took place outside the altar area.
A family photo shows her as a May Queen. She stayed home with her son Mike when the family had only one car.
Peggy went with Barbara and John on the 1993 Alaska cruise and on a family trip to Hawaii (Oahu, Maui and the Big Island).
Every Christmas she set out her silver candy dishes filled with ribbon hard candy; with Buckey she filled in Barbara's twelve place settings of china, crystal and silver after the wedding.
Died on Barbara's birthday, 12 February, aged 96, shortly after Barbara arrived. Barbara gave the eulogy at the family luncheon.
Called 'Granny Quinn' and 'Grandmother'. Barbara and Chuck were the first to call her Grandmother, and 15 more grandchildren followed. Seventeen cousins came to her funeral.
Barbara's grandmother came out west with Buckey and Peggy one time to visit the Adams family.
Died of a heart attack shortly before Barbara's 11th birthday (12 Feb 1959), aged 58 or 59.

Barbara's main babysitter for a year or two and her best friend growing up. He did magic tricks, recited poetry, played the piano, bought doughnuts, fixed up Aunt Pat's bike for her, and every Veterans Day took the grandchildren up Blair Road and bought each one a poppy.
Aunt Pat collected every Elvis Presley 45 rpm record and played all his songs.
Aunt Pat had died by the time Barbara wrote; Barbara remembers her birthday and the anniversary of her death each year.
Barbara mentions 'my aunt Joan Hogan', who went to college with Barbara's 5th-grade teacher Mrs. Cronin. This suggests Joan Quinn married a Hogan.
Aunt Joan had a house in Ocean City, Maryland, where Barbara's family stayed on visits east when it was free.
Aunt Joan had died by the time Barbara wrote; Barbara remembers her birthday and the anniversary of her death.
A regular churchgoer. Her son Buckey went with her every Sunday without fail. She does not appear to have been Catholic.
When Eisenhower asked Theodore McKeldin to be his running mate, he said he would ask the family. Honolulu said no because she distrusted Nixon, so he turned the offer down.
Barbara credits him with some of the best state highways in the country, the urban renewal of Baltimore's Inner Harbor, a new municipal building and slum clearance in Baltimore.
Great uncle Teddy gave young Barbara 'A Child's Book of Bible Stories', one of her favourite books, loved for its colourful pictures.
George and Beryl went to the 1968 Army-Navy game weekend in Philadelphia with John and Barbara. George, an Army man, was pleased when Army won 21-14.
George Sr. was Papa to his grandsons Brian and Brendan, who spent Christmases at Nana and Papa's with cousins George, Geoffrey, Chris and Camille; he took the boys out in his boat on Puget Sound.

On the day Mount St. Helens erupted, Papa, Nana, Aunt Rosemary and Uncle Ralph drove down for Brian's First Communion; hearing the Toutle River had flooded I-5, they left at once for Olympia, and Papa talked the authorities into letting them through.
Papa made cider from the apple trees in his and Nana's front yard.

wells_rosemary.name: Uncle Ralph and Aunt Rosemary O'Dell

facts.value: Ralph, Rosemary and their daughter Louise went to the 1968 Army-Navy weekend and acted as Barbara's chaperones. She stayed in their hotel room and shared a bed with Louise.
Rosemary and her husband Ralph came with Nana and Papa to Brian's First Communion in Kelso on the day Mount St. Helens erupted, then drove back toward Olympia.
Barbara also spells her name Michele.
At Brendan's third birthday in Ocean City, Aunt Michelle spotted him going down the beach, running away from home after being sent for a timeout, so he was quickly caught.
Charlie was born in Monterey, California, while his father was at postgraduate school there.
Charlie was baptized in Monterey by the same priest who had baptized Brian in Meridian, Mississippi, by then chaplain to the naval graduate students.

garret_adams.name: Your son (Brendan's son who graduated in 2021)

facts.value: For Mike and Shelley's wedding, Buckey and Peggy stayed at the Adams house in Kelso, which suggests the wedding was in the Portland area; Barbara spells the bride's name Shelley.
Beryl was Nana to her grandsons Brian and Brendan (with George Sr. as Papa).
After Papa died, Nana went to Hawaii (Maui and Oahu) with John, Barbara, the boys, and Granny and Pops McKeldin.
Nana and Papa had many apple trees in their front yard; Papa made cider and Nana made apple pies.
During their year in Redding, John and Barbara visited Trudy and Mike almost every weekend, leaving Friday night and returning Sunday night; Barbara called them her saving grace in Redding.
On the 2010 Scotland trip Trudy got separated from the group in St. Andrews; when she stood up to wave them over, a seagull stole her pizza.
Trudy also went on a trip to the Big Island of Hawaii with John and Barbara.
The wedding ring set Jack Poleman gave Emily was among her jewelry that Buckey gave Barbara on her 21st birthday; a sapphire was later set into it.

Barbara painted a karate boy rock and a chef rock for Owen, and he is the only grandchild who asked her to knit more sweaters after she made him a sweater and hat; he used to answer 'me too' to 'I love you'.
Barbara painted a 'Gavinator' rock for Gavin, apparently a family nickname for him.
Lola died of cancer after radiation and chemotherapy.
Uncle John had died by the time Barbara wrote; she remembers the dates of his birth and death.
